scope: Leakage audit of the first metric flower VACE export
summary: The v1 VACE data is revoked for held-out evaluation because its edge control and per-clip reference were computed directly from target frames.
evidence: The v1 exporter applied Canny to target RGB and copied each clip's exact middle target frame as its reference input.
Frame-disjoint train/validation splits do not prevent oracle leakage when validation controls contain target pixels.
The corrected exporter uses only calibrated depth, projected stem/contact state, and one separately rendered robot-only identity image.
lessons: Evaluation input independence is a stronger requirement than source-frame split disjointness.
limitations: No adapted-versus-zero-shot result from v1 can support a generalization claim.
next_actions: Re-export all clips from an accepted exact-contact full rollout with target RGB excluded from controls.
